novel_features.name: Citation Snowball Tracker
novel_features.description: Recursively build a citation graph from seed papers, tracking the expanding frontier across sessions so you see exactly which new papers cite your seeds
novel_features.rationale: Requires persistent cross-session graph storage that no stateless E-utility wrapper can provide
novel_features.why_it_matters: When an agent needs to expand a literature review or detect emerging citation clusters around a drug safety signal

novel_features.name: Publication Velocity Monitor
novel_features.description: Track PubMed publication counts over time for a saved query and alert when velocity departs from baseline
novel_features.rationale: Requires historical time-series storage that no E-utility endpoint provides natively
novel_features.why_it_matters: When an agent is monitoring whether a pharmacovigilance signal is gaining traction in the literature

novel_features.name: Offline Abstract Corpus Search
novel_features.description: Full-text search over cached abstracts with FTS5 proximity operators, regex, and BM25 ranking that PubMed itself cannot do
novel_features.rationale: Requires local FTS5 indexing of fetched abstracts; PubMed search operates on MeSH terms, not arbitrary text patterns
novel_features.why_it_matters: When an agent needs proximity search or regex patterns over biomedical text that PubMed search cannot express

novel_features.name: Saved Search Drift Detector
novel_features.description: Compare snapshots of a saved search to show which PMIDs appeared, disappeared, or were retracted since a given date
novel_features.rationale: Requires storing the full PMID result set at each run; PubMed Alerts only track additions
novel_features.why_it_matters: When an agent needs to audit what changed in a literature surveillance query for pharmacovigilance compliance

novel_features.name: Batch Citation Match with Retraction Check
novel_features.description: Resolve a BibTeX or CSV of references to PMIDs via ECitMatch and flag retracted papers in one pass
novel_features.rationale: Chains ECitMatch + EFetch retraction status; prohibitively slow without local caching of resolved mappings
novel_features.why_it_matters: When an agent is validating a manuscript's reference list for retractions or unresolvable citations

narrative.headline: Every E-utility, plus a local database for citation tracking, drift detection, and cross-database queries no other NCBI tool offers
narrative.value_prop: Search, fetch, and link records across PubMed, Gene, Protein, and dozens more NCBI databases. Sync results to a local SQLite store for offline full-text search, citation snowballing, and publication velocity monitoring. The only NCBI CLI with structured JSON output, agent-native design, and persistent state across sessions.

quickstart.comment: Search PubMed and get structured JSON
Fetch a paper's abstract by PMID
Sync all resources to local SQLite for offline use

troubleshoots.fix: Set NCBI_API_KEY for 10 req/s (free at ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/account/settings)

troubleshoots.symptom: Empty results for a query that works on PubMed website
troubleshoots.fix: PubMed website uses automatic MeSH expansion; add [MeSH] field tags to your query

troubleshoots.symptom: EFetch returns XML when you expected text
troubleshoots.fix: Use --format abstract for plain text or --format medline for MEDLINE format
Use sync with --all to paginate through the full result set

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when you need to search PubMed or other NCBI databases from the terminal, track citation graphs over time, run proximity searches that PubMed cannot express, or build reproducible literature review workflows with PRISMA-compliant deduplication.

recipes.title: Find recent papers on a drug safety signal
recipes.command: ncbi-entrez-pp-cli esearch --db pubmed --term "semaglutide AND (thyroid OR medullary)" --retmax 20 --agent --select esearchresult.idlist
recipes.explanation: Search for recent papers linking semaglutide to thyroid concerns, returning only the ID list for efficient agent processing
